title: The Baby and the Bathtub: AI, Science, and the Crisis of Understanding
chineseTitle: 婴儿与洗澡水：人工智能、科学与理解危机
summary: 文章以一篇前沿实验室宣称攻克数学世纪难题的新闻开篇，深入探讨了AI在推动科学狂飙突进的同时，给人类带来的理解危机、学术边界冲突与主体性丧失的深层忧虑。

paragraphs.paragraphTitle: 第一段：引子与背景段（Lead-in & Background）
paragraphs.thesisAndContext: 作者借由一个具体的历史里程碑节点开篇，以极具冲击力的新闻性叙事铺陈事件规模。核心基调由震撼过渡至迷茫与警惕，末句以数学家群体的审慎反应收尾，迅速引出全文对该历史性突破深远影响的追问与探究。
paragraphs.englishText: October 6th, 2026, may be hailed as the most significant turning point in mathematics. An American frontier lab unleashed a torrent of more than 700 papers, professing to have cracked or nudged forward 372 enigmas that had defied researchers for decades. Mathematicians are still trying to figure out what this means for their field.
paragraphs.chineseText: 2026年10月6日，可能会被奉为数学史上最重要的转折点。一家美国前沿实验室抛出了多达700多篇论文的洪流，自称已经破解或向前推进了372个困扰了研究人员几十年的世纪难题。数学家们仍在极力弄清楚这对他们的领域意味着什么。

paragraphs.paragraphTitle: 第二段：基准参考段（Golden Sample）
paragraphs.thesisAndContext: 作者把镜头从数学界拉开，宣布事件的真正意义在数学之外——它迫使整个科学界正视 AI 正在改写科学的根基。
paragraphs.englishText: The impact will reach far beyond mathematics. Science must now come to terms with how artificial intelligence is reshaping its entire foundation. These breakthroughs are a double-edged sword: they mark a great leap forward for humanity and prove the astonishing speed of AI, yet they also caution us against a future where machines decipher a universe that humans can no longer comprehend. The defining question is whether we can push boundaries forward without leaving our own understanding behind.
paragraphs.chineseText: 这一影响将远远超越数学的范围。科学现在必须正视人工智能正在重塑其整个根基的现实。这些突破是一把双刃剑：它们标志着人类的一大跃进并证明了AI惊人的速度，然而它们也告诫我们要警惕这样一个未来：机器解出了人类再也无法理解的宇宙。决定性的问题在于，我们能否在不落下自身理解的前提下推进边界。

paragraphs.paragraphTitle: 第三段：AI 能力的边界与震撼（The Scale of AI Capability）
paragraphs.thesisAndContext: 阐述AI在数学和科学领域的爆发并非偶然，而是算力与算法跃迁的必然结果。
paragraphs.englishText: Mathematics proved to be an ideal testing ground for AI, driven as it is by ironclad logic that computers can verify step by step. Yet the breakthrough hardly ends with pure calculation. As our science reports explore this week, AI is rapidly transforming the practical sciences, largely because they lean on mathematics as a foundation. It has already sharpened meteorological forecasts, envisioned millions of promising new materials, and helped stabilise nuclear fusion experiments. Most remarkably, it has learned to predict the intricate 3D shapes of nearly every known protein from simple amino acids—a triumph that rightfully earned a Nobel Prize.
paragraphs.chineseText: 事实证明，数学是人工智能的理想试验场，因为它由计算机可以一步步验证的铁律逻辑驱动。然而，这一突破远不止于纯粹的计算。正如我们本周的科学报道所探讨的那样，人工智能正在迅速改变实用科学，主要是因为它们以数学为基础。它已经使气象预报更加精准，构想出数百万种极具前景的新材料，并帮助稳定了核聚变实验。最引人注目的是，它学会了从简单的氨基酸预测几乎所有已知蛋白质复杂的3D结构——这一成就实至名归地赢得了诺贝尔奖。

paragraphs.paragraphTitle: 第四段：生物学领域的潜在跃迁（Biological Breakthroughs）
paragraphs.thesisAndContext: 探讨AI在生物学领域的深远应用，如基因编辑与生命模拟。
paragraphs.englishText: Further AI-driven breakthroughs are practically inevitable, and nowhere is the potential more profound than in biology. Researchers are already deploying AI to breed drought-tolerant crops, accelerate drug discovery, and engineer targeted viruses to attack lethal bacteria. At the same time, teams are working to simulate the inner workings of living cells inside silicon. If scientists can truly model life computationally, they may eventually master biology to the point of creating entirely new organisms from scratch. In that world, DNA would look less like a sacred mystery of nature and more like software code—ready to be edited and rearranged by algorithms at will.
paragraphs.chineseText: 由人工智能驱动的进一步突破几乎是不可避免的，而且在生物学领域，其潜力再怎么强调也不为过。研究人员已经在部署人工智能来培育耐旱作物、加速药物研发，并设计靶向病毒来攻击致死细菌。与此同时，各团队正致力于在硅片内部模拟活细胞的内部运作。如果科学家能够真正通过计算对生命进行建模，他们最终可能会掌握生物学，达到从零开始创造全新生物的程度。在那个世界里，DNA看起来将不再像是大自然的神秘圣物，而更像是一段软件代码——随时准备被算法随意编辑和重新排列。

paragraphs.paragraphTitle: 第五段：数学界的震动与反弹（The Backlash from Mathematicians）
paragraphs.thesisAndContext: 以数学界学者对硅谷侵入的反弹为例，剖析人类对“失去理解过程”的抗拒。
paragraphs.englishText: As with so much in AI, this prospect is both exhilarating and deeply unsettling. For many mathematicians, the initial reaction was outright alarm. Ever since OpenAI’s breakthroughs, scholars have fiercely pushed back against what they see as Silicon Valley encroaching on their territory. The Association for Human Mathematics, representing more than 900 academics, warned bluntly that ‘mathematicians did not ask for this work to be done.’ In their view, the true reward of mathematics lies not simply in obtaining a proof, but in the intellectual struggle itself—the very journey that expands human understanding. Allowing machines to generate answers that humans cannot comprehend is like handing students the answer sheet to their homework: without the effort, real learning simply disappears.
paragraphs.chineseText: 正如人工智能领域的许多事物一样，这一前景既令人兴奋又深感不安。对许多数学家来说，最初的反应是彻底的惊慌。自OpenAI取得突破以来，学者们一直激烈地抗击他们所认为的硅谷对自身领地的侵蚀。代表了900多名学者的“人类数学协会”直言不讳地警告说，“数学家并没有要求做这项工作。”在他们看来，数学真正的回报不仅仅在于获得一个证明，而在智力斗争本身——正是这段旅程扩展了人类的理解。允许机器生成人类无法理解的答案，就像是把作业答案直接递给学生：没有了努力，真正的学习也就不复存在了。

paragraphs.paragraphTitle: 第六段：效率与结果的实用主义哲学（Pragmatism over Theory）
paragraphs.thesisAndContext: 反思学术界的自我利益与偏见，主张科学应当追求有效的结果而非神圣化的形式。
paragraphs.englishText: There is more than a hint of self-interest in these complaints. Academics have no exclusive right to decide how knowledge is made, and the search for truth belongs to everyone, not just an academic guild. The traditional scholarly ladder, climbed by solving theorems, is far from sacred. If necessary, it must be reshaped for an era where AI generates the proofs and humans simply evaluate them. In the end, science should not prize theoretical understanding above tangible results. Every time someone takes a painkiller to cure a headache, they rely on a cure that works, even if the exact mechanism behind it remains a mystery.
paragraphs.chineseText: 这些抱怨中不乏有一丝自私自利的意味。学者们并没有决定知识如何产生的独占权，对真理的探索属于每一个人，而不仅仅是一个学术行会。通过求解定理而一步步攀登的传统学术阶梯绝非神圣不可侵犯。如果有必要，必须为人工智能生成证明而人类只需进行评估的时代重塑这个阶梯。归根结底，科学不应将理论理解置于切实的成果之上。每当有人服用止痛药来治头痛时，他们依靠的是一个行之有效的治疗方法，哪怕其背后的确切机制仍然是个谜。

paragraphs.paragraphTitle: 第七段：权力、资源与超级智能的隐忧（The Hidden Perils of Superintelligence）
paragraphs.thesisAndContext: 警示AI公司并非出于慈善投入科研，超级智能一旦失控将导致人类失去驾驶权。
paragraphs.englishText: Yet the anxiety over ceding science to machines is far from groundless. AI companies are not pouring vast resources into research out of pure generosity. Much like human beings, models grow sharper and more capable by tackling hard problems. Many experts believe that any system that excels at scientific reasoning will inevitably excel at almost everything else. If that proves true, competing with the leading AI labs will become virtually impossible. They will hold models capable of continuously upgrading themselves, reaching a level of intelligence beyond human grasp. Nor will these digital minds stay confined to screens: they will step directly into the physical world, operating through humanoid robots or taking direct charge of laboratory instruments, much as Anthropic has already demonstrated.
paragraphs.chineseText: 然而，对将科学拱手让给机器的焦虑并非毫无根据。人工智能公司并不是出于纯粹的慷慨才向研究中倾注大量资源的。就像人类一样，模型通过攻克难题变得更加敏锐和强大。许多专家认为，任何擅长科学推理的系统也必然擅长几乎所有其他事情。如果事实证明如此，与领先的人工智能实验室竞争将几乎成为不可能。他们将拥有能够不断自我升级的模型，达到超出人类理解范畴的智能水平。这些数字思维也不会局限于屏幕上：它们将直接步入物理世界，通过人形机器人进行操作或直接接管实验室仪器，正如Anthropic已经展示的那样。

paragraphs.paragraphTitle: 第八段：文明的宠物化危机（The Threat of Pampered Pets）
paragraphs.thesisAndContext: 探讨文明将决策权完全外包给算法后，人类面临沦为机器“宠物”的终极伦理危机。
paragraphs.englishText: The challenge this poses for science is identical to the one confronting society as a whole. Progress will require us to feed these machines ever more data, energy, and capital. But if we fail to understand what they are actually doing, blindly footing the bill is sheer recklessness—there is no guarantee their objectives will align with our own. Even if developers manage to ‘align’ these models so they cause no harm, a deeper dilemma remains: a civilization that merely waits for algorithms to tell it what to do—whether in the lab or in daily life—is one where human beings willingly reduce themselves to the machines’ pampered pets.
paragraphs.chineseText: 这对科学构成的挑战与整个社会所面临的挑战如出一辙。进步将需要我们向这些机器喂养更多的数据、能源和资本。但是，如果我们不理解它们真正在做什么，盲目地买单就是彻头彻尾的鲁莽——没有任何保证表明它们的目标会与我们的一致。即便开发者设法“对齐”这些模型使之不造成伤害，一个更深层的困境依然存在：一个仅仅等待算法告诉它该做什么的文明——无论是在实验室还是在日常生活中——都是一个人类甘愿将自己贬为机器的宠物的文明。

paragraphs.paragraphTitle: 第九段：保持人类在环路中（Keeping Humans in the Loop）
paragraphs.thesisAndContext: 主张在绝对保证对齐之前，必须坚持“人在环路中”，确保专家主导核心计算资源。
paragraphs.englishText: Some might well accept that trade-off if the reward is, say, wiping out all diseases. Yet until we have absolute certainty that machines and human values are truly aligned, science must always keep a human in the loop. Laboratories should certainly harness AI to crack difficult problems, but critical resources—from physical benches to massive compute—must remain directed by experts capable of truly understanding what the algorithms are doing. This caution will inevitably slow the pace of discovery. But it is an unavoidable price to pay if humanity is to stay in the driver’s seat.
paragraphs.chineseText: 如果回报是，比方说消灭所有疾病，有些人或许很愿意接受这种权衡。然而，在我们拥有绝对确信机器与人类价值观真正对齐之前，科学必须始终让人类保持在环路中。实验室当然应该利用人工智能来攻克疑难问题，但关键资源——从实体实验台到海量算力——必须继续由能够真正理解算法在做什么的专家来指导。这种审慎不可避免地会放慢发现的步伐。但如果人类要保持在驾驶座上，这是必须付出的不可避免的代价。

paragraphs.paragraphTitle: 第十段：学术体制与AI公司的责任重构（Institutional Reconstruction）
paragraphs.thesisAndContext: 呼吁大学、资助机构与AI大厂共同建立透明、负责任的科研新生态。
paragraphs.englishText: In the meantime, a new era of human-steered machine science will compelling academics to rethink their fields from the ground up. Universities must begin to recognise and reward the vital work of steering models, verifying their breakthroughs, and translating their findings into human understanding—granting tenure and prestige on that basis. Funding agencies should distribute research grants with the same priorities in mind. For their part, AI companies must step up as responsible scientific citizens: they must open their discoveries to rigorous peer review, and make their underlying code and methodologies fully transparent.
paragraphs.chineseText: 与此同时，人类主导的机器科学新时代将迫使学者们从头开始重新思考各自的领域。大学必须开始认可并奖励指导模型、验证其突破以及将研究结果转化为人类理解的重要工作——并在此基础上授予终身教职和声望。资助机构在分配研究经费时也应牢记相同的优先事项。就人工智能公司而言，它们必须挺身而出，成为负责任的科学公民：它们必须向严格的同行评议开放其发现，并使其底层代码和方法完全透明。

paragraphs.paragraphTitle: 第十一段：怀疑精神的复兴与历史回响（The Baby, the Bathtub & Nullius in Verba）
paragraphs.thesisAndContext: 全篇收官段，以西方经典谚语“把婴儿与洗澡水一起倒掉”统领小标题，意指不能因噎废食否定机器发现。以英国皇家学会 17 世纪的创始格言 Nullius in verba（不轻信任何人言）强力收笔，告诫世人切勿对机器全盘盲从。
paragraphs.englishText: Verifying and digesting machine-generated results might seem like tedious, thankless work. Yet science done by humans has always been riddled with errors, largely because academics receive little reward for double-checking the claims of their peers. A renewed culture of rigorous verification and healthy scepticism would make science stronger, not weaker. It is worth recalling the founding motto of the Royal Society from the 17th century: Nullius in verba, or ‘Take nobody’s word for it.’ That timeless warning was meant for human authorities—today, it applies just as urgently to machines.
paragraphs.chineseText: 核验并消化机器生成的成果或许看似是一项乏味且吃力不讨好的差事，然而，由人类完成的科学探索一直以来都充斥着漏洞，很大程度上是因为学者在复核同行主张时极少获得回报。一种重新焕发的、注重严苛核验与良性怀疑精神的文化，将使科学变得更加强大，而非更孱弱。值得重温的是17世纪英国皇家学会的成立校训：Nullius in verba，即‘不信任何人言’。那句跨越时代的永恒告诫原本是针对人类学术权威的——而今天，它同样迫切地适用于机器。
